items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Meanwhile the other band that I’ve had since ’91, with Vic Juris, Tony Marino, Jamey Haddad for 10 years, and Phil Markowitz for the first 6, 7 years

ctx.x: Yeah, great cat. Jurg was at a clinic at Advance with me. So was Ernst, and Ernst still, a very good friend. We did it and said, why don’t we play together? So that’s how we started, 2005. And I said, okay, why don’t we get Billy and Ron and see what happens, and so and so. They put us on tour, and that’s how we got together. We made a record. Now we just made a new one. Richie and I suddenly have four or five records coming out this year. It’s just ridiculous. Getting back together again – the band is like the…

best bands he played with. That’s what he says always. We just have a chemistry. Now, after 15, 20 years, with a break and then we came back together, then it’s even more so, because you value it more when you’re older. You’re glad you got it. You don’t think about, oh, I don’t like the way – you go into the positive, not the negative. All things are cool. We’re doing good. We’re up there playing. Let’s just call it that. Be happy. Be cool. So I’m enjoying it very much. When he comes back, we’ll be able to do a…
Even John Abercrombie does not have the recognition that he should have.

items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: part of that Dave Liebman group, since you brought his name up, he really encouraged that kind of movement

ctx.x: Has the role of the main timekeeper changed over the decades? And I guess I should precede that with who do you think is the main timekeeper in the band?

That’s a good question. That’s been thrown around a lot. You know in a lot of ways I could say it’s me, the bass player. But I mean the drummer is basically – he’s the orchestrator you know. He’s creating the colors. But when I’m playing I’m listening hard to where he’s putting the time. So I want to match with him. I want to groove. You know. A lot of our music is groove. There’s other aspects of our music that’s not groove, that’s rubato and up-in-the-air and ethereal and whatever other adjective I can come up…

This will be totally speculative, but you’ve played with some marvelous saxophone players over the years and I’m thinking in my mind comparing like Zoot Sims with Dave Liebman. Zoot Sims probably came early in your career.
